content: 1. Increasing gastric pH will reduce the absorption and effectiveness of oral ampicillin. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both agents. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. 2. Clarithromycin increases the plasma levels and effects of apalutamide by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor the patient. 3. Co-administration of apalutamide with strong CYP3A4 or CYP2C8 inhibitors does not require an initial dosage adjustment. However, dose reduction may be necessary based on patient tolerability. 4. Both arformoterol and clarithromycin can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient. 5. Armodafinil increases the levels and effects of omeprazole by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic enzyme CYP2C19. Clarithromycin also increases armodafinil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 6. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of atazanavir by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor the patient. 7. Omeprazole increases the levels and effects of avapritinib by inhibiting its metabolism via CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor the patient. 8. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of atogepant by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is required. The recommended atogepant dose is 10 mg orally once daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 9. Omeprazole increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting its metabolism via CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor the patient. 10. Both azithromycin and clarithromycin can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient. 11. Clarithromycin decreases the levels and effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor the patient. 12. Clarithromycin decreases the levels and effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. 13. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. 14. Both clarithromycin and bedaquiline can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring, including ECG, is required. 15. Omeprazole decreases the levels and effects of belumosudil by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is required. Increase the belumosudil dosage to 200 mg orally twice daily when co-administered with proton pump inhibitors. 16. Omeprazole increases the levels and effects of belzutifan by inhibiting its metabolism via CYP2C19. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is required. Belzutifan is a CYP2C19 substrate, and co-administration with CYP2C19 inhibitors may increase the incidence or severity of adverse effects. 17. Belzutifan decreases the levels and effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is required. If co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates cannot be avoided, consider increasing the dose of the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate as per its prescribing information. 18. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is required. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. 19. Bortezomib increases the levels and effects of omeprazole by inhibiting its metabolism via CYP2C19. Use caution and monitor the patient. 20. Clarithromycin increases the levels of berotralstat by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. 21. Clarithromycin increases the levels of betrixaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. Reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg orally once, followed by 40 mg orally daily if co-administered with a P-gp inhibitor. 22. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of bexarotene by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor the patient. 23. Clarithromycin decreases the levels and effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor the patient. 24. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of bortezomib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor the patient. 25. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of bosentan by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor the patient. 26. Omeprazole decreases the levels and effects of bosutinib by approximately 45% due to its pH-dependent solubility. Use caution and monitor the patient. 27. Clarithromycin increases the levels of brentuximab vedotin by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor the patient for adverse reactions. 28. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of brexpiprazole by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is required. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If also co-administered with a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. 29. Clarithromycin increases bromocriptine levels by decreasing its metabolism, likely due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor the patient. 30. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of budesonide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Omeprazole decreases the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is required. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent, and co-administration with drugs that increase gastric pH may lead to premature dissolution, affecting drug release and absorption in the duodenum. 31. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of buprenorphine subdermal implants by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is required. If the dose of the concomitant CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should be transitioned to a buprenorphine dosage form that allows dose adjustments. 32. Butabarbital decreases the levels and effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 33. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of buprenorphine long-acting injection by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is required. If signs of buprenorphine toxicity or overdose occur, transition the patient back to a buprenorphine formulation that allows dose adjustments. 34. Butalbital decreases the levels and effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 35. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of calcifediol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is required. CYP450 inhibitors may alter vitamin D metabolism, potentially affecting serum calcifediol levels and its conversion to calcitriol. Adjust calcifediol dosage as needed, and monitor serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact PTH, and calcium concentrations when initiating or discontinuing a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 36. Cannabidiol increases the levels and effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is required. 37. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is required. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 38. Omeprazole decreases the effects of capecitabine by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Retrospective data suggest that elevated gastric pH caused by PPI use may impair capecitabine tablet dissolution and/or reduce absorption. 39. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of capmatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 40. Carbamazepine decreases the levels and effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 41. Omeprazole decreases the levels and effects of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor the patient. 42. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of cariprazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is required. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors requires cariprazine dose reduction. 43. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of cefdinir by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 44. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of cefditoren by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 45. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of cefpodoxime by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Omeprazole also decreases the effects of cefpodoxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. 46. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of cefuroxime by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Omeprazole also decreases the effects of cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. 47. Cenobamate increases the levels and effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is required. 48. Cenobamate decreases the levels and effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is required. 49. Cenobamate decreases the levels and effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is required. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when co-administered with cenobamate. 50. Clarithromycin increases the levels of ceritinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. 51. Omeprazole decreases the levels and effects of ciprofloxacin by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient. The absorption of ciprofloxacin extended-release tablets was slightly diminished (20%) when co-administered with omeprazole. 52. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of cevimeline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 53. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 54. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of cholic acid by decreasing its elimination. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is required. Avoid concomitant use of inhibitors of the bile salt efflux pump (BSEP), as this may exacerbate the accumulation of conjugated bile salts in the liver, leading to clinical symptoms. If concomitant use is necessary, monitor serum transaminases and bilirubin. 55. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of ciclesonide inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 56. Cimetidine increases the levels and effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clarithromycin also increases the levels and effects of cimetidine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. 57. Omeprazole increases the levels and effects of citalopram by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. The maximum recommended dose of citalopram is 20 mg/day in patients taking CYP2C19 inhibitors due to the risk of QT prolongation. 58. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of clevidipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Increased effects of calcium channel blockers may lead to hypotension, edema, decreased heart rate, and acute kidney injury due to reduced renal blood flow. 59. Omeprazole increases the levels and effects of clobazam by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Dosage adjustment may be required, as CYP2C19 inhibitors may increase exposure to N-desmethylclobazam (active metabolite). 60. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of clonazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 61. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of clorazepate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 62. Cobicistat increases the levels and effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 63. Conivaptan increases the levels and effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 64. Clarithromycin decreases the levels and effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. 65. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. 66. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of conjugated estrogens (vaginal) by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. 67. Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of cortisone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. 68. Omeprazole decreases the levels and effects of crizotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor the patient. Drugs that elevate gastric pH may decrease the solubility of crizotinib, reducing its bioavailability. 69. Clarithromycin increases the levels of crizotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Concomitant use of strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. ECG monitoring is recommended, along with monitoring for drugs that may prolong the QT interval. 70. Crofelemer increases the levels of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient.
